records.name: Theater of Witness
records.summary: A testimonial theater group that turns true stories from people whose voices are often overlooked into plays and films, which the storytellers perform themselves.
records.what_you_do: Send a reflection or tribute through the website, book a screening or workshop for the film Grand Young Women by email, or make a donation. A small group of teens and young adults develops new work with the company through partners AFAHO and CAPA, by selection.

schedule.text: There is no regular schedule. The film Grand Young Women can be booked for a screening or workshop by email, and new productions are announced on the website.

cost.text: The site lists no fee for a screening or workshop. The group asks for tax-deductible donations.

first_step.how: Email teya@theaterofwitness.org to book a screening or workshop for Grand Young Women, or send a reflection through the website form.
first_step.basis: The site lists no drop in events, classes, or volunteer roles, and the teen group works by selection, so the public way in is booking a screening by email and the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Grand Young Women is a 30 minute film made with five girls of African heritage from the African Family Health Organization. The site does not say how a screening or workshop is run, how long it lasts, or what it costs, so ask when you book.
first_visit_tips: Book by email, since the site lists no phone number or office hours.
The office is at 1315 Walnut Street, Suite 300, but the site gives no hours for it.
To take part before a screening, send a reflection through the website form.

records.notes: The site has no volunteer, class or open rehearsal pages. The mailing list link on the home page is malformed (it begins with http://https://), so it is not recorded. The GrandWomen project page gives no performance dates. AFAHO and CAPA are named partners and appear in leads_only.

records.name: Theatre Exile
records.summary: A nonprofit theatre in South Philadelphia that stages new and provocative plays. Its education programs include school residencies and camps, and volunteers and ushers can help at the theatre.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as an usher or in the office, which also gives free entry to shows, or join the education programs (school residencies and camps). An open house on Sunday, October 11, 2026, 3 to 6 pm, is open to visitors, with an RSVP link on the site.

schedule.text: Productions run through a season each year (the 2026 to 27 season is called Season 30). Usher and volunteer shifts are set per show, and the page lists no shift dates.

cost.text: Single show tickets are sold separately, and a 3-show Flex Pass starts at $45. Students and seniors 65 and up get $10 off single tickets with ID, and residents of ZIP codes 19145, 19146, 19147 or 19148 get $5 off with ID. Ushers and volunteers see shows for free.

access.notes: Ask the Box Office in advance about special seating for an access need. Subscription series seating is general admission. Nearest SEPTA: the Broad Street Line (Orange) stop at Tasker-Morris, about two blocks away on foot. Access Card holders can get two $5 tickets for some Preview dates of subscription shows; the company is not part of the LiveArts ACCESS program.

first_step.how: Fill in the online volunteer and usher form linked from the site, or RSVP for the open house on Sunday, October 11, 2026 (3 to 6 pm) and ask about ushering there.
first_step.basis: The usher and volunteer form is open to the public, ushers see shows for free, and the open house is a public stop by, but the site does not say it welcomes newcomers by name or describe training, so it is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: Ushers help at productions and volunteers help in the office, and both see the shows for free. The page does not say how long a shift runs, whether there is training, or how often shifts come up, so ask when you apply. The open house on October 11 is a free stop by event with popcorn and pizza, a good chance to ask about ushering.
first_visit_tips: Arrive at least 30 minutes early, since seating opens about 20 minutes before curtain.
Street parking nearby is free but some spots have a 2 hour limit; the municipal lot at 12th and Reed Streets is about a 2 minute walk and often fills up.
If you will be late, call the Box Office at 215-218-4022 so the House Manager can plan for you.
Turn off electronic devices before the show.

records.notes: Schedule days (Sunday), times (daytime) and the note that shifts are set per show were carried over from tier 1. The pages read today do not confirm them and list no shift dates, so check before relying on them. Workshop pages show only 2022 and 2023 sessions and are not used. The Paper Wings residency partner schools are in leads_only. The volunteer form is a Google form linked from the join page; the general manager's email is on that page and was not recorded.

records.name: Theatre in the X
records.summary: A free theater company in West Philadelphia that stages productions for the African American community and gives chances to playwrights, actors, directors, and behind-the-scenes crew.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free production. You can also audition, volunteer, or work with the group, such as in stage crew, sound, or DJ roles, through the form on the website.

schedule.text: There is no regular schedule. The site lists no show dates, so check the website or the mailing list for the next free production.

cost.text: Productions are free. The company says it aims to offer its shows at no cost to West Philadelphia and the African American community.

first_step.how: Fill in the audition, volunteer, or work with us form on the website and name the role you want, such as stage crew, sound, or DJ.
first_step.basis: Productions are free and open to the public, and one form covers auditions, volunteering, and work roles, but the site lists no dated events or newcomer details to judge a first visit by.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. Many past productions were staged outdoors in Philadelphia parks, several of them free, so for a park show bring your own chair. The group says it works with actors, playwrights, directors, stage managers, sound engineers, and DJs, so name the role you want on the form.
first_visit_tips: Check the website or mailing list for the next free production, since show dates are not listed on the site.
Name the role you want on the form, such as stage crew, sound, DJ, or playwriting.
For outdoor park shows, bring your own chair; past free outdoor shows asked audiences to do so.
Call 484-326-2596 if you want to ask before filling in the form.

records.notes: No 2026 productions are listed anywhere on the site. The newest dated entry is December 2025 on the production history page, which is the basis for last_sign_of_life. The For Colored Girls page gives August dates with no year, so it is not used for status or schedule. The contact email is hidden in the page text, so none is recorded.

records.name: Tikkun Olam Coordinating Team at Germantown Jewish Centre
records.summary: A volunteer team at Germantown Jewish Centre, a synagogue, that follows up on election security and voter protection. It holds Zoom sessions where people talk through local actions they can take.
records.what_you_do: Share voter education, learn about poll worker and poll watcher roles, and talk through local actions. Members can bring their own ideas.

schedule.text: Sessions are held on Zoom and announced one at a time. No regular meeting schedule is posted.

cost.text: The session page does not list a cost. Ask the office.

first_step.how: Call the synagogue office at 215-844-1507 or email office@germantownjewishcentre.org to ask about the next election session and how to get the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The session page is written for members and does not say whether others can attend, so the way in is to ask the office first, even though prospective members are welcome to call and visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: A recent session ran on Zoom for 90 minutes, from 7 to 8:30 pm, where the team reviewed possible actions and decided which ones neighbors might take on together. The page does not say how many people attend or whether guests are welcome. Ask the office before you plan to join.
first_visit_tips: Ask the office whether the next session is open to people who are not members.

The session page names four partner groups: ACLU of Pennsylvania, Committee of Seventy, Election Protection, and the Philadelphia Neighborhood Networks Action Network. Read what each one offers before you come.
The session page asks people to RSVP by email to get the Zoom link, so the office can point you to the right person.

records.notes: Changed from tier 1: audience is now members only and newcomer rating is 2, because the session page is written for members and does not say non-members may attend. The congregation does say prospective members are welcome to call and visit. The session page gives a volunteer's personal email for RSVP; it was left out of this record on purpose. The membership information page returned a 404, so membership details came from the join page. The Chesed (caring) committee of the same congregation has meal delivery and visiting roles; it is a committee, not a separate group, so it is not recorded here. The four partner groups are in leads_only.

records.name: TILT Institute for the Contemporary Image
records.summary: A photography center in North Philadelphia that runs gallery shows, printing services, artist residencies, and youth education for photographers and image makers at every level.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery for free, book a one to one photo tutorial, or ask about the youth programs. Membership opens the Studio, a members only printing space booked by reservation. The artist residency is paid, but applications were closed when the site was read.

schedule.text: Gallery open Wednesday to Saturday, 12 to 6 pm. The members only Studio is open Wednesday and Thursday 12 to 3 pm and Friday and Saturday 12 to 6 pm, by reservation.

cost.text: Gallery visits and free programs cost nothing. Photo tutorials cost $105 to $150 an hour on a sliding scale. Memberships run $60 to $500 a year, or $5 to $40 a month. The members only Studio is $20 an hour with a two hour minimum, plus $4 per square foot for ink when printing.

first_step.how: Stop by the gallery at 1400 N. American Street, Suite 103, any Wednesday to Saturday between 12 and 6 pm to see the current show.
first_step.basis: The gallery is free and open to anyone during posted hours, and each tutorial has a booking link, but the Studio is members only and expects working knowledge of its software, so the site does not invite beginners and the rating is not higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: Gallery visits are self guided: you walk through the exhibitions during open hours at no charge. Tutorials are booked with an instructor in blocks of 1, 1.5, or 2 hours, at $105 to $150 an hour on a sliding scale. The Studio needs a membership and an orientation form first.
first_visit_tips: Gallery hours are Wednesday to Saturday, 12 to 6 pm, so plan the visit inside those hours.
To book a tutorial, contact Danielle Morris, who handles scheduling, at 215.232.5678.
Before using the Studio, new users fill in an orientation form, and the site expects you to know your printing software; a tutorial is offered if you need one.

records.notes: The page at the artist-lab address is titled The Studio and says it is members only, by reservation, so the record uses the Studio name in place of the tier 1 Artist Lab label. Dated events on the home page, not used in the schedule: Eco-Social Realism (September 10 to November 21, 2026) and Still Moments of Everyday Life (December 10, 2026 to February 27, 2027).

records.name: Timoteo Sports
records.summary: A youth sports and mentoring group based on West Hunting Park Avenue in Philadelphia. It runs fall basketball and girls volleyball for kids, a free music program for teens, and after-school and mentoring work.
records.what_you_do: Families register kids for fall youth basketball (ages 6 to 14) or girls volleyball. Teens register for the free DASH Music Program (ages 12 to 18). The group also runs Timoteo LinkUp mentoring for students and lists scholarships with partner schools.

schedule.text: Programs run in seasons. Fall programs: youth basketball on Saturdays 9 am to 1 pm, girls volleyball on Saturdays 9 to 11 am, and the free DASH Music Program on Mondays 4 to 6 pm for eight weeks. Check the site for each season's dates.

locations.label: Timoteo Sports office (DASH Music Program)
locations.address: 1300 W Hunting Park Ave., Philadelphia PA 19140

cost.text: The DASH Music Program is free. Girls volleyball is $55 for a six week Saturday program. The site does not state a basketball fee, and it mentions scholarships without amounts.

first_step.how: Register through the form for the program you want (youth basketball, girls volleyball, or the DASH Music Program), or email info@timoteosports.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Each program has a public registration form and the volleyball listing says all skill levels are welcome, but the site does not describe tryouts or what a first session is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes basketball as structured practices, competitive play, and mentorship, with no tryouts listed. Girls volleyball meets on Saturday mornings at International Christian High School, which the site does not give an address for. The site does not say how long each session runs or what the first practice looks like.
first_visit_tips: Register through the form for each program; the site lists no drop in visits.
Basketball meets at Esperanza, 4261 N 5th St; the DASH Music Program meets at the office, 1300 W Hunting Park Ave.
Ask the office for the street address of the volleyball location, since the site gives only the school name.
Call (609) 200-1351 or email info@timoteosports.org; the contact page also has a form.

records.notes: Scholarships are offered to eligible athletes at three partner schools, with no amounts or application route on the site, so those schools are in leads_only rather than recorded here. The after-school program is marked coming soon with no year and is not recorded. The volleyball fee and Saturday times come from the sports page and match the fall 2026 dates on the home page. Basketball has no published fee.

records.name: Tindley PHL
records.summary: A church-based soup kitchen on South Broad Street that serves dinner to people and families facing financial hardship, with volunteer sign up on its website.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the sign up link on the website, or subscribe to the newsletter to hear when meals and events are planned.

schedule.text: Meals are served on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and the church hopes to serve dinner on more weekdays. The site does not list meal times.

cost.text: The church's site does not state a cost. A public food directory lists the meal as free but says to confirm.

first_step.how: Sign up through the Volunteer Here link on the soup kitchen page, or subscribe to the newsletter on the home page.
first_step.basis: The volunteer sign up and newsletter are public and easy to find, but the site gives no meal times, guest details, or shift details, so the first visit is hard to plan from the site alone.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a meal visit or a volunteer shift, and meal times are not published. The church says it serves meals on Tuesdays and Thursdays and hopes to add more weekdays. Call before you come to confirm the days, the times, and whether a first time volunteer can join a shift.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-735-0442 before you come, since meal times are not on the site and directory listings are unconfirmed.
The site gives no entry rules or check in steps, so ask about them when you call.
Subscribe to the newsletter on the home page to hear when meal days or events change.

records.notes: Directory listings disagree with the church. A public directory entry (feedam.org, a Plentiful listing) shows Tuesday and Thursday hours of 22:30 to midnight, which looks like an error, says current services have not been independently confirmed, and says walk in rules are unconfirmed. The church's own page still says meals are served Tuesday and Thursday. A search result described a February 2025 news report saying the kitchen still needed to reopen; that report could not be opened, so nothing from it is recorded. Confirm the meal schedule by phone before publishing a visit plan. Tier 1 set audience faith to protestant; the soup kitchen page does not limit meals by faith, so that field was removed. A food pantry at the same church (Monday and Wednesday, 11:30 am to 12:30 pm) appears on WhyHunger, which is undated and not on the church's own site, so it is not recorded.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used (Tindley meal times, result inconclusive). 30 WebFetch calls across the 7 groups, well under the 60 cap. One fetch returned 404 (the Tikkun membership information page, which is only linked from site navigation) and one failed with a DNS error (6abc.action.news, a news report surfaced by the search). No bot checks, 403s, paywalls or rate limiting were seen. Verdicts: 7 publish. Carried-over tier 1 fields were kept unless noted in the record notes: Tikkun audience changed to members and newcomer rating to 2; Tindley audience faith removed and cost level set to unknown; Theatre in the X and TILT names and tags corrected to what the pages say; Theatre Exile and Timoteo schedules kept to what repeats. Partner organizations named on the group sites are in leads_only with a null URL, because the pages published no link to them, so none were fetched; they still need research. Volunteer personal emails shown on the Tikkun and Chesed pages were left out on purpose.
